To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lobular carcinoma in Situ (LCIS) is not a true preinvasive lesion, but is a marker for increased risk of developing invasive breast cancer, that the risk is not uniform, but is dependent on the location of LCIS within the breast, that LCIS is not a marker for aggressive disease, and that LCIS is associated with increased risk for ipsilateral invasive cancer.
the risk of local failure in patients with breast cancer and Lcis at the surgical margins is low.

The risk of local failure in patients with lobular in situ carcinoma (LISCA) at the final surgical margin is 1.4%, and that this risk is not significantly different from the risk of local failure of patients with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) or invasive carcinoma (IC) at the final margins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the development of an effective and efficient algorithm for the analysis of breast cancer images.
the development of new and more effective methods of cancer treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of local recurrence is increased in breast cancer patients who present with LCIS.
lobular carcinoma in-situ (LCIS) is a risk factor for invasive breast cancer and that LCIS should be treated with a bilateral mastectomy.

the use of the term “Lobular Carcinoma In Situ” is appropriate in the diagnosis of a breast lesion that is composed of small, round to oval cells that are cytologically similar to the cells of invasive lobular carcinoma, that is present in the terminal duct lobular unit (TDLU) in an architectural pattern of either a single focus or a cluster of foci, and that is not present in the stroma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a 2-step procedure for breast-conserving surgery (BCS) with a 2nd procedure in case of positive margins, is associated with a low risk of local failure and a low re-operation rate, even in cases with lobular carcinoma insitu (LCIS).
the risk of local recurrence is low in patients with LCIS at the surgical margin, regardless of margin width.
the risk of local recurrence is low for patients with LICS in the final margin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of lobular carcinoma in-situ (LCIS) at the final surgical margin in patients with breast cancer is not associated with increased risk of local failure (LF), and that the presence of invasive cancer at the margin is the only significant risk factor for LF.

the risk of local failure in patients with breast cancer and lobular carcinoma in-situ (LCIS) at the final surgical margin is low, even in patients with a positive margin, and re-excision is unlikely to be beneficial.
lobular neoplasia (LN) at the surgical margin is associated with a higher risk of local recurrence in patients with breast cancer.
